sum: STI sinks 2%; Nikkei dives over 6% into bear market; AEM slides more than 9% after the previous day’s 20% loss
[SINGAPORE] Singapore-listed technology stocks fell on Friday (Nov 6), tracking a global rout in technology and semiconductor stocks.
The Straits Times Index (STI) was also down by more than 2 per cent in early trade. As at 9.04 am on Friday, the benchmark index was down 120.51 points, or 2.3 per cent, at 5175.74 points.
All STI counters had dropped, with Yangzijiang Shipbuilding leading the decline. The counter was down 8.4 per cent, or S$0.39, at S$4.26 as at 9.48 am.

The banks were similarly trading lower on Friday morning. OCBC , which reported its Q3 financial results before trading, was down 0.3 per cent while DBS and UOB were down 2.2 per cent and 2 per cent as at 9.55 am, respectively.

Across the broader Singapore market, technology stocks posted some of the steepest declines on market open. As at 9.07 am, shares of AEM slid 9.3 per cent to S$5.78, while UMS Integration declined 8.4 per cent to S$1.63.
Frencken shed 7.6 per cent to S$1.70, while CSE Global slipped 6.7 per cent to S$0.84.

sum: [SINGAPORE] The following companies saw new developments that may affect trading of their securities on Thursday (Nov 5):

DBS : The lender reported on Thursday a net profit of S$2.81 billion for the three months ended Sep 30, down 5 per cent from S$2.95 billion in the year-ago period. DBS said earnings growth was offset by lower markets trading income amid unfavourable equity market conditions. The latest net profit fell short of the S$2.95 billion consensus forecast from a Bloomberg survey of eight analysts. DBS also announced that its chairman, Peter Seah, will retire at the end of this year, with board member Anthony Lim set to succeed him from Jan 1, 2027. Shares of DBS ended 0.1 per cent or S$0.10 lower at S$70.78 on Wednesday.

Centurion Accommodation Reit (CAReit) : The real estate investment trust (Reit) on Wednesday posted net property income of S$117.7 million for the nine months ended Sep 30, coming in 4.8 per cent above its prospectus forecast. Its manager said the better-than-expected performance was helped by higher rental rates at its Singapore worker dormitories and new bed capacity. Revenue came in at S$164.4 million, 5.7 per cent ahead of the S$155.6 million forecast in the Reit’s initial public offering prospectus dated Sep 18, 2025. Units of CAReit ended 1.9 per cent or S$0.02 higher at S$1.07 on Wednesday, before the announcement.

DBS Group stock heads for November 5 earnings as profit forecast dips
sum: DBS Group is heading into a closely watched third-quarter earnings release on Thursday, November 5, 2026. A MarketWatch earnings preview published on November 2 said analysts expect profit to edge lower while total income increases.

A consensus of nine analysts polled by Visible Alpha points to third-quarter net profit of SGD 2.93 billion, down 0.7 percent from the year-earlier period. Six analysts expect total income to rise 2.7 percent to SGD 6.09 billion.

The forecast suggests that revenue growth may not fully offset pressure on the bottom line. Jefferies analysts cited normalizing fees and weaker market-related income as potential offsets to resilient non-interest income. Maybank Securities analyst Thilan Wickramasinghe said softer equity markets and higher bond yields may have weighed on trading income.

Investors are expected to focus on DBS's wealth management business, which has supported earnings in recent quarters. The bank is targeting assets under management of SGD 1 trillion in the segment, making client flows and recurring fee generation important indicators for the results and the outlook.

The earnings release should also clarify whether loan growth and interest-sensitive income can cushion pressure on margins. Credit costs, capital returns and cost control will be relevant for assessing the durability of the bank's profitability as interest-rate conditions evolve.

Management's comments on the 2026 and 2027 outlook are likely to receive close attention. The market will be looking for indications on net interest income, wealth fees, trading income and the pace at which profitability can adjust to changing rates.
DBS Group stock traded at 49.29 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 09:39 CET on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Investors can use the real-time quote of DBS Group stock for the latest market indication.

sum: DBS Group stock is heading into its third-quarter earnings release with analysts expecting a modest decline in profit. The bank is scheduled to report on Thursday, November 5, 2026.

DBS Group stock traded at 49.92 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 15:15 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026. That was 2.29 percent below the 51.09 euros quoted in our October 31 report at 10:18 CET, a separate comparison from the daily exchange-market move.

A MarketWatch earnings preview published on November 2 said a consensus of nine analysts polled by Visible Alpha points to third-quarter net profit of 2.93 billion Singapore dollars, down 0.7 percent from the year-earlier period. Six analysts expect total income to rise 2.7 percent to 6.09 billion Singapore dollars.

The outlook suggests that revenue growth may not fully offset pressure on earnings. Jefferies cited normalizing fees and weaker market-related income, while Maybank Securities analyst Thilan Wickramasinghe pointed to softer equity markets and higher bond yields as possible drags on trading income.

Investors will focus on wealth management and the bank's progress toward its 1 trillion Singapore dollar assets-under-management target. Fee generation and client asset flows could help cushion pressure on interest-sensitive income.

Management's comments on the 2026 and 2027 outlook will also shape the next valuation debate. The release should provide fresh evidence on margins, fee income, capital returns and the ability to control costs as credit conditions remain in focus.

DBS Stock Drops 0.91% on Friday, Testing Support Level
sum: On October 30, 2026: price 73.13 SGD, trend downtrend, RSI 33.1, support 73.13, resistance 78.56. technical analysis of dbs stock. DBS Stock Drops — full…

DBS Group closed at S$73.13 on Friday, October 30, 2026, down 0.91% for the session and 1.76% over five days. The stock is close to its three-month low of S$72.50 while its decline continues, putting the focus on whether selling pressure eases near the bottom of the recent range. The latest session’s volume was 1.3 times its 20-day average, while on-balance volume fell—a sign that heavier trading has not yet confirmed a shift in demand.

The short-term structure remains weak. DBS traded below its 20-day moving average of S$74.66, which itself fell 1.29% over five days, and below its 50-day average of S$76.23. No new moving-average crossover was reported. The lack of a fresh crossover does not alter the underlying message: price and the shorter-term average remain beneath the longer-term reference, while the short-term average is declining.

The price sat at the bottom of its 20-trading-day range, between support at S$73.13 and resistance at S$78.56. The three-month low of S$72.50 is nearby, but proximity to a low is not, by itself, evidence of a reversal. The session’s close also matches the stated 20-day support level, making the next response around this zone especially relevant.
As shown in the chart, price is positioned below both moving averages and near the lower part of the recent range.

The indicators show weakness, but not a uniform signal of an established rebound. The RSI is 33.1, classified as neutral in the supplied data; it is close to the lower end of the scale, but does not independently confirm a turn. The Stochastic is oversold, with %K at 14.5 and %D at 34.1. That can occur when selling has been persistent; an oversold reading is not a timing signal unless price and momentum begin to recover.

The MACD remains negative: at -0.766, it is below its -0.708 signal line, and its histogram is -0.058. This points to negative momentum rather than a confirmed bullish divergence. Taken together, the readings suggest the stock may be stretched near support, while the broader momentum picture still leans downward.

Bank sell-off casts pall in Southeast Asia, Singapore stocks drop 3%
sum: (Oct 8): Major banks in Southeast Asia declined more than 1% on Thursday, with the region's top lender, DBS Group, dragging Singapore stocks more than 3% lower as rising bond yields brought into focus risks to bank earnings growth and funding costs.
The MSCI EM Asia equities index declined 1.8% in its worst day since early September, largely weighed down by a 2.6% drop in South Korea's Kospi.

In Singapore, the FTSE Straits Times index shed as much as 3.2% to hit its lowest since mid-July, with DBS dipping 5.2% to mark its steepest daily loss since April last year. Smaller rivals OCBC and UOB fell nearly 5% each. Together, the three banks account for more than half of Singapore's main index, and make up more than a third of the MSCI Asean equity gauge, which marked its worst daily drop since early March.

JPMorgan and Citi raised concerns over Asean banks' earnings outlook, citing surging long-dated bond yields, higher funding costs and the normalisation of exceptional first-half wealth-related income.

"A combination of higher rates, AQ (asset quality) risks, funding tightness and capital-market-related revenue risks should impact quite a few bank stocks going into 3Q results," JPMorgan analysts led by Harsh Wardhan Modi wrote.
They recommend trimming exposure to all three major Singapore banks.
After a strong run in bank shares, investors may have become more sensitive to earnings risks and negative catalysts, said James Ooi, market strategist at Tiger Brokers.

$8 billion wiped off OCBC value as shares slide 5.8% in heavy trade, Money News
sum: SINGAPORE - Shares of OCBC dropped as much as 5.8 per cent in intraday trading on Wednesday (Oct 7).
As at 11.11 am, the counter was down 5.2 per cent or $1.66 at $30.54. By the trading break, the counter had slipped further, down 5.8 per cent or $1.85 to $30.35 at 12.30 pm.
It was also the top traded stock by value, with over 14.8 million shares worth over $459 million changing hands at that time.
OCBC's value dropped from close to $145 billion on Tuesday, to about $136.4 billion as at 12.30 pm.

Citi downgraded the stock from "neutral" to "sell" in a banking note on Wednesday morning, with a target price of $27.50. It expects OCBC's Q3 earnings to be flat year on year, and growth optimism for the lender to be derailed.

This year OCBC has had the steepest jump in its valuation, with its price-to-earnings multiple expanding by 46 per cent. Citi noted that OCBC is trading at the tightest dividend yield spread over bond yield at 70 basis points.

Citi noted the market's misplaced optimism on Singapore interest rates and OCBC's exceptional first-half wealth related income. It expects third-quarter net interest margin to contract because of higher Singapore-dollar fixed deposit (FD) rates of 35 to 70 basis points.
